findings.F1: The fade's next-day gain beyond the coin's mean daily return depends mostly on the day of the move: after Sunday moves it is 0.00424 (t 4.89, n 4304), after Saturday moves 0.00177 (t 2.60, n 4303), and after Tuesday moves 0.00307 (t 3.65, n 4314), while Wednesday, Thursday and Monday sit near zero (|t| ≤ 0.33).
findings.F2: Friday moves continue rather than reverse: the fade gain after a Friday move is −0.00189 (t −2.95, n 4301), the only weekday with a significantly negative value.
findings.F3: The reversal sits only where 20-day volatility is high against its 120-day level: in the top tercile of vol20/vol120 the fade gain is 0.00296 (t 4.04, n 6056), against −0.00023 (t −0.36) and 0.00026 (t 0.41) in the lower two terciles.
findings.F4: Moves made on heavy volume reverse more, which is the opposite of the brief's thin-book claim: in the top tercile of the day's volume over its 30-day median the fade gain is 0.00170 (t 2.66, n 9145), against 0.00005 (t 0.11) in the bottom tercile.
findings.F5: The edge is real before costs but smaller than the cost of trading it: mean timing gain is 0.000452 per bar against a mean fee of 0.000647 per bar, so the book's mean daily return is −2.7e-05 (Sharpe −0.03).
findings.F6: The reversal has faded in recent years: the fade gain is positive with t above 2 in 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2023 (0.0045, 0.0040, 0.0036, 0.0018), but negative in 2024 (−0.00126, t −1.79) and 2025 (−0.00094, t −1.42), and the book's daily mean is lowest in 2024 (−0.00177, t −1.89).
findings.F7: The fade works better in falling markets: when the coin's 20-day return is negative, the fade gain is 0.00160 (t 3.35, n 15538), against 0.00048 (t 1.11, n 14584) when it is positive.

ideas.idea: A coin's move over the weekend (Saturday and Sunday, UTC) is followed by a move the other way over the next day, and the larger the weekend move, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade weekend moves into Monday only, sized by the size of the move, and trade far less often than a daily fade so fees no longer eat the edge.
ideas.name: Weekend move fades Monday

ideas.idea: A coin's Friday move continues in the same direction over the next day, and the larger the Friday move, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow rather than fade a coin's Friday move into Saturday, sizing with the move.
ideas.name: Friday move continues Saturday

ideas.idea: A coin's daily move is followed by a move the other way over the next day, and the higher its 20-day volatility relative to its 120-day volatility, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade daily moves only in proportion to how far short-term volatility has risen above its longer-run level, and would leave most days untraded.
ideas.name: Vol-spike daily move reversal

ideas.idea: A coin's daily move is followed by a move the other way over the next day, and the higher that day's volume relative to its 30-day median, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade moves made on heavy volume more strongly than moves on quiet days.
ideas.name: High-volume move reverses

ideas.idea: A coin's daily move is followed by a move the other way over the next day, and the more the coin has fallen over the past 20 days, the larger the move back.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade daily moves harder in coins that have been falling over the past 20 days.
ideas.name: Downtrend daily move reversal
